paper.title: An Improved Parametrization and Analysis of the EXP3++ Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic regime (multiarmed bandit with losses in [0,1])
settings.definition_quote: In this regime the losses $\ell_t^a$ are sampled independently from an unknown distribution that depends on $a$, but not on $t$. ... We also make the standard assumption that the losses are bounded in the $[0,1]$ interval.

algorithms.name: EXP3++ with unweighted-loss LCB gap estimation (xi_t(a) = beta ln t / (t DLCB_t(a)^2))

source.label: thm:EXP3++
source.quote: Let $\xi_t(a) = \frac{\beta \ln t}{t \DLCB_t(a)^2}$, where $\DLCB_t(a)$ is the empirical gap estimate from Algorithm~\ref{algo:IWUCB}. Then for $\alpha = 3$ and $\beta = 256$ the expected regret of \EXPPP in the stochastic regime satisfies \[ R_t = O\lr{\sum_{a:\Delta(a)>0} \frac{\lr{\ln t}^2}{\Delta(a)}} + \tilde O\lr{\sum_{a:\Delta(a)>0} \frac{K}{\Delta(a)^3}}, \] where the $\tilde O$ notation hides logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Mixed O + O~ statement; recorded as O_tilde over the sum (the first term is actually O without hidden logs). Regret is defined via means in the stochastic regime (pseudo-regret). eta_t from the EXP3++ parametrization (proof uses eta_t >= (1/2)sqrt(ln K/(tK))). Same algorithm keeps the 4 sqrt(K t ln K) adversarial guarantee of SS14 (cited).
